content: Ṣāʾin al-Dīn says that on his first trip to Herat he fell in with a prominent master who was effusive in affection but whose disciples behaved unacceptably; he admonished him privately, and the shaykh was receptive, disavowed a number of his disciples and set about correcting their belief in the Mahdi's imminent advent, which the learned masters hold to lie far in the future.
